sources.scope: Motivating question and attributed bounded exceptional-width constructions.
Crosspost, Misha Lavrov's partial width-five answer, and attribution to earlier width-three work.
Established background on transfer-based enumeration of grid Hamiltonian cycles; not cited as a proof of the proposed classification.
Misha Lavrov's 25 October 2025 explicit 2k square-grid construction and forced-zigzag uniqueness argument.
Misha Lavrov's 17 November 2025 comment extending to even lengths and proposing reflection for odd lengths; source of the all-length upper-bound idea.
Jacobsen (2007), Section 2: established frontier connectivity and premature-cycle rejection background, not the present cutoff or eventual-equality theorem.

Đokić, Doroslovački, and Bodroža-Pantić, The Structure of the 2-factor Transfer Digraph for Linear Grid Graphs: prior outlet-word component classification by odd/even imbalance. Its states omit path pairings and admit disjoint cycles; it does not supply the present Hamiltonian cutoff.
de Gier, Loops, matchings and alternating-sign matrices, Section 2.1, Equation (1): established adjacent reconnection of noncrossing matchings.

Kazazi, Reconfiguration of Hamiltonian Cycles in Rectangular Grid Graphs (2026), Introduction main theorem: at most mn^2 valid double-switch moves between complete cycles when n>=m. Related polynomial reconfiguration of complete cycles, not a theorem about column-appending frontier-pairing connectors or entrywise transfer multiplicities.

Bodroža-Pantić, Kwong, Pantić (2015), exact positive-window B-state model, quotient weights, endpoint sets, and Conjecture1/Questions1–3 addressed by the cylinder application. Small published matrices and sets are factual expected data in the independent checker.

Beaton–Eng–Soteros (2016), Section4.1: prior qualitative strong connectivity for realizable Hamiltonian 1-patterns carrying pair partitions, by concatenating containing polygons using the Theorem6 construction. No exact correspondence to the 2015 B-state model is imported.
Đokić–Doroslovački–Bodroža-Pantić (2023): later binary outlet-word 2-factor transfer model, distinct from the 2015 Hamiltonian window-label graph.

Filomat38:1 (2024), Definition3 and Theorem5 concern binary 2-factor component structure. Lemma3, pp64–65, uses a local-code involution inducing bitwise outlet complement and the odd-width component isomorphism. Relevant prior symmetry method; different state semantics from the exact 2015 Hamiltonian B-state graph.

Transactions on Combinatorics13:1 (2024), printed p43: describes the motivating thin-cylinder asymptotic phenomenon as conjectural. Bounded literature context; not evidence excluding all earlier or later solutions.

attribution_refinement.upper_construction: Misha Lavrov's 25 October 2025 square-grid answer gives the 2k cap/forced-zigzag construction. Transpose and row reflection match the square specialization here. His 17 November 2025 rectangular-grid comment gives the even-length extension and proposes reflection for odd lengths. The included note is a self-contained checked reconstruction of that prior work; no construction or parity-extension priority is claimed.
attribution_refinement.frozen_source_scope: The five earlier mathematical source snapshots retain their exact bytes. The README and provenance add the Beaton–Eng–Soteros pairing-state connectivity context. The new cylinder source includes that attribution directly.
attribution_refinement.transfer_background: Jacobsen (2007), Section 2, describes frontier connectivity information and premature-cycle rejection. These are established methods, not claimed innovations of this project. The 2-factor outlet-word classification of Đokić, Doroslovački, and Bodroža-Pantić is related prior work with different state semantics. Adjacent matching reconnection is standard, as in de Gier, Section 2.1, Equation (1).
attribution_refinement.realizable_pairing_connectivity: Beaton–Eng–Soteros (2016), Section4.1, supplies prior qualitative strong connectivity for patterns occurring in Hamiltonian polygons. This is closer pairing-state prior work than the binary outlet quotient. The new application explicitly proves its own state correspondence, actual-state lifting, and endpoint-exchanging symmetry; no literature-wide priority is claimed.
attribution_refinement.two_factor_complement_symmetry: Đokić–Doroslovački–Bodroža-Pantić, Filomat38:1 (2024), Lemma3, pp64–65, already use the coordinatewise involution (a f)(b e)(c d) on local 2-factor codes, inducing binary outlet complement and the odd-width component isomorphism. This is prior complement-symmetry methodology. It does not establish the fixed-pairing shade flip on actual 2015 Hamiltonian B-states, the B4 endpoint exchange, or equal even-width leading amplitudes. The README and provenance add this credit while preserving the reviewed mathematical source.
